content:
Last Friday (21st), the verdict in the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China case was delivered. In the early hours, police escorted a woman who was queuing to attend the hearing onto a police vehicle and took her away. In response to enquiries, the police stated that the woman was arrested on three charges: "disorderly conduct in a public place", "resisting or intentionally obstructing police officers in the execution of their duties", and "seditious intent".

Around 5am last Friday, more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During this time, a plainclothes police officer pointed out that a woman in the queue was "suspected of wearing a top with somewhat seditious intent", and escorted her onto a police vehicle. While taking the woman away, several officers kept directing journalists to leave, saying "take you to the press area", and pulled the orange cordon line towards the direction of Ying Wa Street. After the woman boarded the police vehicle, they put away the cordon line. On that day, a "court-watcher" who was queuing near the woman said she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese characters printed on it.

"集誌社" (Collective) enquired with the police about the reasons for the woman being taken away and whether she had been arrested. The police replied this morning (24th) that they had conducted a security operation in the area around the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts on 21 August, during which a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "disorderly conduct in a public place", "resisting or intentionally obstructing police officers in the execution of their duties", and "seditious intent", and was detained for investigation.
